definitions.explanation: A communal Chinese cooking style where a simmering pot of broth is placed at the center of the table, and diners cook raw ingredients in it. Often served with a divided pot offering two broth flavors.

notes:
Originally a Chinese dish ({火锅|ひなべ} in Chinese), it has become widely popular in Japan. The defining feature is a pot of boiling broth kept simmering at the table, into which diners dip thinly sliced meat, vegetables, tofu, and noodles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {火鍋|ひなべ}⟦{専門店|せんもんてん}→専門店：15924_senmonten⟧ — hot pot restaurant
- {火鍋|ひなべ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{囲|かこ}む→囲む：02037_kakomu⟧ — to gather around a hot pot
- {火鍋|ひなべ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{具材|ぐざい}→具材：06230_guzai⟧ — hot pot ingredients
- {薬膳|やくぜん}{火鍋|ひなべ} — medicinal herb hot pot

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{鍋|なべ}→鍋：01038_nabe⟧ — pot; hot pot (general Japanese term for any communal pot dish)
- ⟦しゃぶしゃぶ→しゃぶしゃぶ：10479_shabushabu⟧ — shabu-shabu (Japanese-style hot pot with thin meat slices)
- ⟦すき{焼|や}き→すき焼き：10368_sukiyaki⟧ — sukiyaki (sweet soy-based Japanese hot pot)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese ⟦{鍋|なべ}→鍋：01038_nabe⟧ (hot pot) culture has existed for centuries, but {火鍋|ひなべ} specifically refers to the Chinese style, distinguished by its intensely spiced broth (often with Sichuan peppercorns and chili oil) and the split-pot ({鴛鴦鍋|おしどりなべ}) format. Many Chinese-style {火鍋|ひなべ} restaurants have opened across Japan in recent years.
